gp.text: Product gross profit and gross margin percentage increased significantly during the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 compared to the same periods of 2025, primarily as a result of higher sales prices due to the current supply-demand environment discussed above and product sales mix.

cor.text: Total gross margin percentage increased from 4% during the third quarter of 2025 to 66% in the same period of 2026, primarily due to license fee revenue under the Samsung License Agreement, which has no associated cost of sales, and higher product gross margin. Similarly, total gross margin percentage increased from 4% during the first nine months of 2025 to 36% in the same period of 2026 for these same reasons.

rd.text: Research and development expenses increased during the three and nine months ended September 26, 2026 compared to the same periods of 2025, primarily due to higher employee headcount and the associated increase in overhead costs. We expect research and development expenses to increase in future periods as we invest to support growth in our products business.

ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses increased during the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 compared to the same periods of 2025 primarily due to a $6.1 million increase in stock-based compensation expense, primarily related to the Chief Executive Officer Performance Equity Award granted in July 2026, higher corporate legal expenses, and sales commissions associated with higher sales. We expect our selling, general and administrative expenses will increase in future periods as we invest to support growth in our products business, expand our customer base, and when, if and as we recognize additional compensation expenses related to the Award and the retention bonuses for our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer approved in November 2026 and described in Note 10 to the condensed and consolidated financial statements.

tax.text: We recorded an income tax benefit of $44.0 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, compared to no provision for income taxes in the corresponding periods of 2025. The provision primarily relates to Korean withholding taxes on license fee payments under the Samsung License Agreement, which Samsung is required to gross up, and U.S. federal and state income taxes on taxable income from the license and settlement arrangements, after utilization of available net operating loss carryforwards. During the third quarter of 2026, we released $56.5 million of valuation allowance because we concluded it is more likely than not that the related deferred tax assets will be realized from projected taxable income, and we continue to maintain a $23.0 million valuation allowance against deferred tax assets we do not expect to realize. We will reassess our valuation allowance and estimated annual effective tax rate each quarter as projections change.

Net product sales.text: In addition, the vast majority of our net product sales in recent periods have been generated from resales of products sourced from SK hynix pursuant to the Product Purchase and Supply Agreement with SK hynix, which was entered into on April 5, 2021 (the “SK hynix Supply Agreement”). The term of the supply provisions of this SK hynix Supply Agreement expired in April 2026. We continue to purchase products from SK hynix following expiration of the SK hynix Supply Agreement on a purchase order basis on similar terms to the prior SK hynix Supply Agreement, but SK hynix ultimately may not continue to supply us with products for resale on similar terms or at all. In such circumstances, our financial results, including our revenue, profits and margins in future periods may be adversely affected. In August 2026 and as noted above, we entered into the SSI Supply Agreement with Samsung Semiconductor providing us with the right to purchase up to $300 million of DRAM and NAND products per year for an aggregate of up to $1.5 billion over a five-year term. Should Samsung fail to comply with the terms of this agreement and the related arrangements, our financial results of operation would be adversely affected.

License fee.text: Our patent litigation with Samsung and Micron has been resolved pursuant to the Samsung Agreements and the Micron Agreements, and a significant portion of our near-term revenue and cash flow is now expected to be derived from license fees and net sales pursuant to these agreements. As a result, our results of operations and liquidity will depend on Samsung’s and Micron’s performance of their payment and supply obligations. Other proceedings, including our appeals to the CAFC, ex parte reexaminations at the USPTO, and our litigation with Google, remain pending, and we account for any potential recoveries from these matters as gain contingencies that are not recognized until realized. See “Legal Proceedings” in Part II, Item 1 of this report and See Note 6 to the condensed consolidated financial statements included in Part I, Item 1 of this report for more information.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

The information contained in, or accessible through, our website is not part of, and is not incorporated by reference into, this Form 10-K. Investors should not rely on any such information in deciding whether to purchase our common stock.

Our ability to sustain profitability will depend on increased revenue growth from, among other things, increased demand for our product offerings and our ability to monetize our intellectual property.
Our pursuit of this strategy depends on our ability to obtain and protect our patents, which is governed by an uncertain process.
Our ability to maintain or increase our product sales to our large or key customers also depends on a variety of factors, many of which are beyond our control.

Even once a customer has qualified and begins purchasing our products, if the products fail to meet applicable quality standards, our customers may discontinue purchases from us until we are able to resolve the quality issues that are causing these failures, which we may not be able to do.
We depend on third parties to design and manufacture for our products and the component products we resell, which exposes us to risks.
We rely on third parties to manufacture our products, the products we resell and, in some instances, to design or manufacture, the products we sell or resell.

Further, we may not be able to redesign the customized components used in our products to be manufactured by a new manufacturer, in which case we could infringe on the intellectual property of our current design or manufacturing partner when we manufacture the products with a new design or manufacturing partner.
We depend on certain key employees, and our business could be harmed if we lose the services of any of these employees or are unable to attract and retain other qualified personnel.
Our future success also depends on our ability to attract, retain and motivate highly skilled engineering, manufacturing and other technical and sales personnel.

We rely on our internal and third-party sales representatives to market and sell our products and the component products we resell, and any failure by these representatives to perform as expected could reduce our sales.

We also rely on information technology systems and networks, including third-party "cloud-based" service providers, to process, transmit and store electronic information in connection with our business activities.

The U.S. Congress has enacted laws, and the SEC has adopted rules, requiring disclosure of specified minerals, known as conflict minerals, that are necessary to the functionality or production of products manufactured or contracted to be manufactured by public companies.
We rely on a combination of patent protection, trade secret laws and restrictions on disclosure to protect our intellectual property and other proprietary rights.
